decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the ductility and toughness of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through various methods such as composition change, processing or synthesis route, thermal or thermomechanical treatment, microstructure architecture, and surface or interface engineering. Earlier studies have shown that the addition of certain elements, such as oxygen or nitrogen, can improve the damping capacity and mechanical strength of HEAs. Other studies have demonstrated that the use of advanced processing techniques, such as selective laser melting or high-pressure and high-temperature treatment, can enhance the strength and ductility of HEAs. Recently, researchers have explored the use of stepwise thermo-mechanical processes to generate ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory high-entropy alloys.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in improving the ductility and toughness of HEAs, there is still a need to develop a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms and to identify the most effective methods for achieving simultaneous improvements in strength and ductility. decision.why: The addition of certain alloying elements, such as Cr or Ti, has been shown to improve the strength and ductility of HEAs.
